subject: Materials Science
title: Pitting Corrosion: Invisible Holes
description: One-minute skill: Pitting Corrosion: Invisible Holes.

hook.text: A stainless steel tank looks perfect outside — but a tiny pit has already punched through the wall.

buildup.text: Pitting corrosion creates small, deep holes — highly localized attack that's hard to detect.

discovery.text: Chloride ions break down the passive film at weak points — once a pit starts, it accelerates itself.

twist.text: Inside a pit, pH drops and chloride concentrates — creating an aggressive environment that digs deeper.

climax.text: Water mains fail from pitting after decades — a few tiny holes flood streets while 99% of the pipe is fine.

punchline.text: One tiny hole can defeat an entire structure — pitting is corrosion's sniper.

quiz.question: What makes pitting corrosion particularly dangerous?
options: It creates deep, localized holes that are hard to detect
